dialogue.content: worked out I've paid for something twice for two months.
sat through a very small dip without doing anything.
took cash out and then used the card anyway.
read the terms properly before signing up. once.
I assumed doing nothing in a downturn would be the calm option. it isn't — with no action taken I check it constantly, and somewhere around week three I do something large and unplanned.
I'd have said doing nothing costs nothing. it costs a great deal of attention.
did the shop with a list and stuck to it.
looked at the projection graph and felt nothing.
set aside something small for a thing months away.
made a planned rebalance in a calm month.
checked three accounts in a row out of habit.
worked out the cost per use of something. justified it.
got paid and did nothing about it for four days.
compared this month to last month and stopped comparing.
put a card in a drawer as a strategy.
the downturns I came through without damage were the ones where I'd made one small planned move early on. having already acted, I stopped watching it.
the small move mattered that much?
not for the money. for the watching.
checked a bill I already knew the amount of.
added up subscriptions on a napkin. stopped at nine.
checked the balance and closed the app again.
moved a direct debit date by three days.
